findings.title: The workflow bypasses rather than minimally repairs the confirmed read-only-copy mutation boundary
evidence: .github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:179-190 copies and archives cache_root without first making the source cache recursively read-only.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:249-253 performs cp -a, rm, then chmod read-only in diagnosis; it has no writable transition on the disposable negative tree before rm.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:297-301 repeats cp -a, rm, then chmod read-only in offline verification; it has no writable transition before rm.

benchmarks/external-oss-v6/tests/v6-contract-validation.mjs:57 checks an unused $cache spelling rather than $cache_root, and lines 58-60 require cp/rm/read-only but not the required writable-negative transition.
The fresh G0 reproducer still confirms that source chmod read-only before cp -a preserves non-writable parent modes and makes host rm fail for all three required paths.
findings.impact: The implemented sequence is writable source, writable copied negative tree, removal, then read-only. It does not preserve the source/cache read-only boundary while minimally making only the disposable negative tree writable for host removal, so it does not implement the accepted root-cause repair contract.
findings.requiredRepair: Keep the source/cache tree read-only, explicitly make only the disposable negative tree writable before host-side removal, verify the required path is absent, and restore that negative tree read-only before its read-only cache mount. Update the contract test to require this exact order and the actual variable names.

findings.title: Unreadable cache does not produce the required DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE code
evidence: .github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:328 maps a missing required path to DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE, but line 329 maps an unreadable required path to CACHE_READ_DENIED.
benchmarks/external-oss-v6/tests/v6-permission-regression.mjs:12 derives DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE only from existsSync=false, and line 40 tests only a removed path.
The independent semantic check reported workflowUnreadableCode=CACHE_READ_DENIED and regressionUnreadableCacheCase=false.
findings.impact: The explicit G1 contract that an unreadable dependency cache fail closed as DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE is neither implemented nor regression-tested.
findings.requiredRepair: Map an unreadable required cache entry to DEPENDENCY_CACHE_INCOMPLETE and add a regression that creates an existing but unreadable cache entry and asserts that exact code.

findings.title: The required negative-removal fail-closed regression is absent
evidence: benchmarks/external-oss-v6/tests/v6-permission-regression.mjs:28-33 copies a writable cache tree; line 35 makes only the source required directory read-only after the copy.
benchmarks/external-oss-v6/tests/v6-permission-regression.mjs:38 removes the still-writable negative entry successfully, and line 39 makes the negative root read-only only after removal.
The test does not inject EACCES/EPERM or another denied removal, does not assert the workflow aborts when removal fails, and contains none of TASK-OSS-01, TASK-OSS-03, or TASK-OSS-09.
The independent semantic check reported regressionNegativeReadonlyBeforeRemoval=false, regressionAssertsDeniedRemoval=false, and regressionTaskIds=[].
findings.impact: Although set -e plus the post-removal existence check make the shell implementation statically fail closed, the specifically required regression does not protect that behavior or establish the same negative-cache contract for all three tasks.
findings.requiredRepair: Add a denied-removal case that proves nonzero removal leaves the target present and causes the qualification path to fail, then exercise or table-drive the exact contract for all three task IDs.

findings.title: Uploaded failure evidence collapses the structured diagnostic codes
evidence: .github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:294 overwrites diagnostics.json with OFFLINE_PERMISSION_CAUSE_UNKNOWN for every nonzero shell exit.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:318-336 emits specific codes inside the container, but lines 351 and 355 redirect those outputs under the runtime root.
.github/workflows/external-oss-v6-dependency-cache.yml:369-371 uploads only cache-receipt.json and diagnostics.json, not the redirected positive or negative output containing the specific code.
benchmarks/external-oss-v6/tests/v6-contract-validation.mjs:62-64 verifies only that code strings occur somewhere in workflow source.
findings.impact: A runtime failure would publish the generic unknown code rather than the structured cause produced by the harness, so the structured failure-code contract is not realized in reviewable G1 evidence.
findings.requiredRepair: Preserve the specific sanitized harness or host failure code in diagnostics.json and test the resulting uploaded diagnostic contract, while retaining a bounded unknown fallback only for genuinely unclassified failures.

acceptanceCriteria.result: The G0 host-side read-only-copy mutation root cause is independently confirmed, but the PR does not implement the required minimal writable-negative/read-only-source sequence.
Exactly the five required jobs exist in the required order.

No secrets, environment gate, Codex, hidden oracle, or provider execution is present; permissions are contents read. Network activity is confined to public pre-runtime seed/cache preparation. The Docker commands statically specify network none, read-only rootfs, UID/GID 65532, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, read-only cache/harness, and only /workspace, /tmp, and /home/benchmark as writable binds. No chmod 777, container root user, or skipped smoke was found. None of these Docker properties was runtime-accepted.

Five job structure and a real GitHub Actions Docker integration implementation exist, but unreadable-cache classification, denied-removal regression coverage, and reviewable structured failure diagnostics are deficient.

Committed G1 evidence is text-only and sanitized; no credential, hidden oracle, Codex result, external-service result, cache archive, virtualenv, dependency tree, or runtime image is committed. The local Docker limitation exactly states EXPECTED_NOT_RUN: LOCAL_DOCKER_DAEMON_UNAVAILABLE and docker info independently failed because the local daemon socket is absent. The workflow also hard-codes that local-only literal in its GitHub-hosted diagnosis receipt without checking daemon availability; this receipt has not been produced or accepted.

Fresh local/static checks and current PR checks are recorded separately from runtime. The workflow_dispatch-only Docker integration has not run in this review, and no G1 runtime acceptance or READY cache claim is made.
